data.body_html:
When planning a boat rental on the Costa del Sol, two names come up repeatedly: Marbella and Benalmádena. Both offer beautiful Mediterranean waters, but the value you get for your money differs significantly. This Marbella vs Benalmádena boat rental cost comparison breaks down the real costs, inclusions, and hidden extras so you can make an informed choice.

Upfront pricing: Marbella’s all-inclusive vs Benalmádena’s add-ons

The most striking difference is pricing transparency. In Marbella, every charter from [Boat Rental Marbella](/blog/marbella-boat-rental-vs-benalmadena-cost-comparison/) includes the skipper, fuel, drinks (water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava), light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and 21% Spanish IVA. The price you see is the price you pay.

For example, our Tier A boats — the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) — cost €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours, all-inclusive. In Benalmádena, a similar-sized boat might advertise €500 for 2 hours, but then add €150 for fuel, €100 for a skipper, and 21% VAT, bringing the total to over €900. That’s 20% more for less.

Fleet quality and variety

Marbella’s fleet is larger and more premium. We operate 16 boats from Puerto Banús, including luxury yachts like the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax, €4,719 for 4 hours with a free jet ski), the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax), and the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax). Benalmádena has fewer superyachts and generally older models.

If you want a speedboat, we have the Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) and a 7m speedboat (6 pax). For sailing, the Lagoon 380 catamaran (11.6m, 10 pax) is available. Benalmádena’s fleet is more limited, especially for larger groups.

Proximity to the best coves

Location matters. From Puerto Banús, you can reach Cala del Faro in 10 minutes and Cala Cortés in 20 minutes. From Benalmádena, the same coves take 30-40 minutes. That extra cruising time eats into your charter, meaning less time swimming, sunbathing, and enjoying the sea.

Marbella also offers easy access to Cabopino, Estepona, and the Golden Mile coastline. Benalmádena’s marina is closer to Fuengirola and Mijas, but the coves are less sheltered and can be crowded.

Hidden costs and surprises

We’ve already touched on fuel and skipper fees, but let’s be specific. In Benalmádena, many operators charge a fuel deposit (often €200-€300) that you may or may not get back. Some also add a cleaning fee (€50-€100) or require a damage deposit of €500-€1,000. Marbella rentals from us have no such extras. The price includes everything, and we only ask for a security deposit on larger yachts, which is fully refundable.

Weather and sea conditions

Both destinations enjoy the same Mediterranean climate, with 300+ sunny days per year. However, Marbella’s coastline is more sheltered by the Sierra Blanca mountains, reducing the effect of the Poniente and Levante winds. Benalmádena can experience choppier seas, especially in the afternoon, which can affect comfort and safety.

Which is better for your budget?

If you’re looking for the best value, Marbella wins hands down. The all-inclusive pricing means you can budget accurately without surprises. For a family of 5, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) is a great choice — pricing on request via WhatsApp, but still fully inclusive. For a larger group, the Bandido (11.5m, 8 pax) or Fairline Targa 12m (10 pax) offer excellent value.

Benalmádena might suit you if you’re on a very tight budget and willing to negotiate, but the final cost often exceeds Marbella’s transparent pricing. For luxury seekers, Marbella’s fleet of superyachts — like the Canados 86 (26m), K80 (24m), and Maiora 26m — is unmatched.
